text:
anya: heads up — onboarding NebulaX-lite q4 on int8 we saw a weird token merge affecting ja/ko tests. small but consistent BLEU drop on subtitle set.

devin: can you paste an example?

anya: sure. reproducer below. note the halfwidth katakana + hangul jamo combo gets tokenized as one token on the quant build but splits on fp16.

anya: ```
input: "今日はﾊﾝｶｸｶﾀｶﾅ와 가는 테스트입니다."
fp16 decode: "今日はﾊﾝｶｸｶﾀｶﾅ와 가는 テストです."
int8 decode: "今日はﾊﾝｶｸｶﾀｶﾅ와가는 テストです."
```

hao: ugh the join between the katakana halfwidth (hankaku) and the following hangul jamo collapses? that would shift token boundaries and scoring. :thinking_face:

mari: what's the delta on BLEU and is it localized to this tokenization mismatch or a sampling change?

anya: small sample: overall BLEU -0.9 on subtitles (n=2k). when we filter to examples containing mixed-script boundaries it's -3.4.

eval-bot: quick-run reports:
- fp16 baseline run: BLEU 28.7
- int8 on NebulaX-lite: BLEU 27.8
- tokenization mismatch examples (n=132): BLEU 21.2 -> 17.8

devin: thanks. can you run tokenized diffs? i want to see token ids around the boundary.

anya: sending token dump for one sample:
```
fp16 tokens: [ ... 9543, 120, 4078, 77, 912 ... ]  // 120 = HANKAKU-KATAKA placeholder
int8 tokens: [ ... 9543, 120, 4078_912_combine, ... ] // combined token id on int8 runtime
```

hao: that combined id smells like a changed tokenmap after quant kernel folding or a tokenizer->vocab mismatch at mapping time. did we use the same tokenizer + merges file?

anya: yes same tokenizer artifact sha. difference only in model loading path: int8 build used kernel-merged vocab remap during offline convert.

mari: could be our convert script's bytepair normalizer dedupe step that tries to compress rare subtokens and accidentally created a merged entry. Did we run the same convert flags?

anya: convert flags: `--merge-rare --fold-width --force-remap` on int8. fp16 used `--force-remap` only.

devin: try rerunning convert without --merge-rare and do a smoke decode. If that fixes it, we should avoid aggressive merge for multilang models.

anya: doing that now, will run minimal eval.

sre-tim: ping — if this is a conversion flag thing, we should block the int8 rollout to dedicated until triage. SLA customers might hit this in production. :eyes:

anya: agreed. stop int8 canary for NebulaX-lite. setting tag `hold-int8-rollout` and posting to release-war-room.

eval-bot: rerun (no --merge-rare) results:
- int8 rebuilt: BLEU 28.5
- tokenization mismatch examples: BLEU 21.0 -> 20.8

mari: nice — that strongly implicates --merge-rare. likely it merged a halfwidth+hangul combination as a new subtoken.

hao: action items: 1) roll back int8 canary, 2) patch convert pipeline to disable --merge-rare for multilang, 3) add a unit test for mixed-script boundary preservation, 4) run full eval across ja/ko/zh.

devin: i'll own the unit test + convert patch. anya can you coordinate the rollback and re-run the full eval when done?

anya: yes. rollback in progress. posting minimal release note in release-war-room.

mari: also add a metric to Optimize that flags any changes to average token boundary alignment on mixed-script slices. will help catch this earlier.

hao: good call. adding to Optimize backlog.

anya: TL;DR: false positive regression caused by aggressive merge step during int8 convert. rollback done, patch queued, on full eval run. thanks all. :thumbsup:
